title: Main Line with 3...Qa5
intro: After 2.exd5 Qxd5 3.Nc3, retreat to a5. Build a rock-solid set-up with ...Nf6, ...c6, ...Bf5 and ...e6, and handle White's early threats.

lessons.title: The ...c6 and ...Bf5 set-up
lessons.summary: Retreat to a5, play ...Nf6 and ...c6, and bring the bishop out to f5.

steps.text: White develops with tempo against your queen. The classic square for the queen is a5.
Retreat your queen to a5, keeping pressure on c3 and e1.
steps.hint: Move the queen to the a-file.
steps.ifRight: From a5 the queen stays active and clears d5.

steps.text: Develop your king's knight towards the centre.
steps.hint: Put the g8 knight on f6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Nf6 to control d5 and e4.

steps.text: Support d5 and give your queen a path back to c7.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...c6 so your queen can tuck into c7 if attacked.
steps.ifRight: Now Black is ready for ...Bf5 and ...e6.

steps.text: White develops quietly with 6.Be2. Bring your light-squared bishop out before closing the chain with ...e6.
steps.hint: Put your c8 bishop on f5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...Bf5 so your bishop stays active outside the pawn chain.

lessons.title: Meeting 6.Ne5 and 5.Bd2
lessons.summary: Drop the bishop back to e6 after 6.Ne5 Bf5 7.g4 and sidestep 5.Bd2 with ...Qb6.

steps.text: Instead of 6.Bc4, White sometimes jumps forward with 6.Ne5 to eye c4 and f7.
Keep developing your light-squared bishop cleanly.
steps.hint: Bring the c8 bishop to f5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...Bf5: after 7.g4, your bishop steps back to e6.
steps.ifRight: Notice that 7.Nc4 can be met by 7...Qc7.

steps.text: Step back to a square where the bishop cannot be trapped.
steps.hint: Not g6: there h4 and h5 would trap the bishop. Go to e6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...Be6: on g6 the bishop would be caught by h4 and h5.
steps.ifRight: The bishop is safe on e6, and White's g4 push has loosened the kingside.

feedback.f5g6: 7...Bg6 walks into 8.h4, and h5 traps the bishop. Go to e6.

steps.text: Watch out if White plays 5.Bd2 before Nf3, setting up a discovered attack on your queen. Put your queen on an active square.
steps.hint: Move your queen to b6, hitting both b2 and d4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...Qb6 (or 5...c6): 5...Qb6 steps out of the pin and attacks b2 and d4.
steps.ifRight: Black sidesteps the discovered attack and puts pressure on b2 and d4.

steps.text: If White plays 6.Bc4, develop your bishop outside the pawn chain before playing ...e6.
steps.hint: Put your c8 bishop on f5.

lessons.title: Meeting 4.b4 (Leonhardt Gambit)
lessons.summary: Take the pawn with 4...Qxb4 and tuck the queen on d6 after 5.Rb1.

steps.text: Some aggressive players try the Leonhardt Gambit (4.b4), offering a pawn to open the b-file.

steps.hint: Capture on b4 with your queen.
steps.ifRight: Now White will chase your queen with 5.Rb1.

steps.text: Tuck the queen onto a safe central square where it eyes the kingside and stays out of trouble.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...Qd6 (or 5...Qa5): on d6 the queen is safe and guards the kingside.
steps.ifRight: Black is a clear pawn up and develops ...Nf6 and ...c6 smoothly.

steps.text: White develops 6.Nf3. Keep developing solidly to consolidate your extra pawn.
steps.hint: Develop your king's knight to f6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...Nf6 (followed by ...a6 or ...c6) to keep White's pieces out.
steps.ifRight: Black keeps the extra pawn and finishes development cleanly.

steps.text: If White skips d4 and plays 4.Bc4, continue developing smoothly.
steps.hint: Develop your king's knight to f6.
steps.ifRight: Black reaches the same sturdy Scandinavian set-up.
